notes.printed: "(exact, post hoc; … puzzles)" marks a bootstrap interval that collapsed to one value (every puzzle right, or every one wrong), replaced by the exact two-sided 95% Clopper–Pearson interval from free analysis 4 (post hoc; it changes no test). The count in the mark is the number of puzzles, not of samples (the conservative unit).

Panel 1 gives the pooled tests in the three views; its readings are per view, and a test holds only if it is no worse in all three views (TAB-10). The three views agree to every printed digit because no refusal or truncation touched either side of a test.

Panel 1's ties-counted-wrong row for Test B2 is post hoc (free analysis 13): the vote is scored as deployed, except that a vote whose top answers tie, the right one among them, scores nothing instead of an equal share; d and its paired bootstrap interval only, with no p and no reading, and B2's reading is unchanged. A tie that included the right answer decided
6-sample votes (a mean over puzzles, each over all of its possible votes; three-against-three ties alone
1.15%); such a tie decided at least one vote in
puzzles (in either shape). TAB-02 gives the tie-decided share for Tests 1–3.
